definition_zh: adj. 可传染的；可传达的
definition_en: able to be passed from one person to another
core_image: 拥挤车厢里一个人咳嗽，周围的人下意识后退
scene: 这种病在密切接触者之间可以传染。The disease is communicable between close contacts.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：communicable 指可传染的；句意是这种病在密切接触者之间可以传染。

senses.title: Able to spread between people
senses.definition: able to pass from one person to another, as a disease
senses.definitionCN: 像疾病那样能从一个人传给另一个人
senses.example: Measles is highly communicable.
senses.exampleCN: 麻疹传染性很强。
senses.why: Latin communicare means to share.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 communicare 意为共享。

senses.title: Able to be passed on as knowledge
senses.definition: able to be communicated as an idea or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 可作为想法或情感被传达
senses.example: Good writing makes complex ideas communicable.
senses.exampleCN: 好的写作让复杂想法变得可传达。
senses.why: The sharing root covers both disease and ideas.
senses.whyCN: 「共享」词根同时覆盖疾病与思想。

intro.en: Communicable comes from a Latin verb meaning to share.
intro.cn: communicable 源自拉丁语「共享」的动词。

items.en: Communis means shared or common.
items.cn: communis 意为共同的。

items.en: Communicare means to share or impart.
items.cn: communicare 意为分享、传达。

items.en: The adjective means able to be shared.
items.cn: 该形容词意为可分享的。

items.en: English used it of ideas first.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语先用它说思想。

items.en: It now mainly describes disease.
items.cn: 现代医学中主要形容疾病。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the commun- shape; the near-meaning group names how disease spreads.
note.cn: 形近组共享 commun- 词形；近义组列出疾病传播的说法。

The sharing of information.
Willing to talk.
Spread by contact.
Caused by germs that spread.

normalIntro.en: Whatever can be shared can be communicable.
normalIntro.cn: 能被共享的东西，都可以是 communicable。

normal.en: Communis means shared.
normal.cn: communis 意为共同的。

normal.en: Communicare means to share.
normal.cn: communicare 意为分享。

normal.en: A shared illness is communicable.
normal.cn: 可共享的病就是可传染的。

normal.en: A shared idea is communicable too.
normal.cn: 可共享的想法也就是可传达的。

normal.en: Doctors use it for disease.
normal.cn: 医生用它形容疾病。

abstract.en: A cough in a crowded car.
abstract.cn: 拥挤车厢里的一声咳嗽。

abstract.en: A story passed mouth to mouth.
abstract.cn: 口耳相传的故事。

abstract.en: A seed carried by wind.
abstract.cn: 被风带走的种子。

examples.en: The illness is communicable before symptoms appear.
examples.cn: 这种病在症状出现前就可传染。

examples.en: Tuberculosis is a communicable disease.
examples.cn: 结核病是一种传染病。

examples.en: The feeling was communicable without a word.
examples.cn: 这种感受无需言语也能传达。

dict_mnemonic.text: communicate（传达）+ -able（能…的）→ 能被传出去的，即可传染、可传达的。

root: 拉丁 communis（共同）→ communicare（分享）→ communicabilis → 英语 communicable

sensesIntro.en: One word for a shared germ and a shared idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个词既指共享的病菌，也指共享的想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cough in a crowded carriage
core.cn: 核心意象：拥挤车厢里的一声咳嗽

branches.en: A cough passing down a row.
branches.cn: 沿一排乘客传开的咳嗽。

branches.en: A school closing for measles.
branches.cn: 因麻疹停课的学校。

branches.en: A feeling passed without words.
branches.cn: 不用语言传达的感受。

branches.en: An idea that travels well.
branches.cn: 易于传播的想法。

branches.en: Something shared, whether germ or thought.
branches.cn: 被共享之物，无论病菌或思想。

intro.en: Communicable is built from sharing pieces; the list adds spreading words.
intro.cn: communicable 由「共享」词素构成；下面列出传播词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin communis is shared, communicare is to share, and contagio is contact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis 意为共同的，communicare 意为分享，contagio 意为接触。

latinEntries.exampleCN: communicare 产生 communicate 与 communicable。
communis 产生 common 与 community。
contagio 产生 contagious 与 contagion。

definition_en: to share information or feelings with others, or to be connected through an opening or passage
core_image: 两端之间架起一条能让意思顺利通过的电话线
scene: 她用手势和眼神把意思传给对面的同伴。They communicate through short messages every day.
sceneCN: 这里 communicate 指「交流；传达」（第 1 个义项：交换信息）；句意是他们每天靠短消息交流。

senses.title: To share information
senses.definition: to give and receive information with other people
senses.definitionCN: 与他人互相传递和接收信息
senses.example: The two teams communicate by radio.
senses.exampleCN: 两队之间用无线电联络。
senses.why: The Latin root meant to share, and sharing information is its first job.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为分享，而分享信息正是它最首要的功用。

senses.title: To express feelings
senses.definition: to make your thoughts or feelings known to others
senses.definitionCN: 让他人知道你的想法或感受
senses.example: Music can communicate joy without words.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐不用词语也能表达喜悦。
senses.why: What is shared is not only facts but also feelings.
senses.whyCN: 被分享的不只是事实，还有感受。

senses.title: To be connected
senses.definition: to be joined through a door, passage or opening
senses.definitionCN: 通过门、通道或开口相连
senses.example: The two rooms communicate through a narrow door.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个房间通过一扇窄门相通。
senses.why: Rooms that connect let things pass, just as people let meaning pass.
senses.whyCN: 相通的房间让东西通过，就像人与人之间让意思通过。

intro.en: Communicate comes from Latin communicare, to share, from communis, common.
intro.cn: communicate 来自拉丁语 communicare（分享），词根是 communis（共有）。

items.en: Communis meant shared by all, and communicare meant to share.
items.cn: communis 意为众人共有，communicare 意为分享。

items.en: Communicare also covered making something common to two parties.
items.cn: communicare 也指让某物为双方所共有。

items.en: French communiquer carried the sense of passing news along.
items.cn: 法语 communiquer 带有把消息传递出去的含义。

items.en: English communicate first meant to share or impart.
items.cn: 英语 communicate 最初表示分享或传授。

items.en: It widened to telephones, letters, gestures and connected rooms.
items.cn: 它的用法扩展到电话、书信、手势以及相通的房间。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers longer verbs near the shape of communicate, while the meaning group lists verbs of passing meaning on.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 communicate 形状相近的较长动词，近义组列出传递意思的动词。

entries.definition: to honour the memory of someone
to make something harder
to prepare land for crops
to make an idea understood
to give part of something to others
to exchange letters or messages

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line carrying meaning, then move to feelings that travel and rooms that connect.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一条传递意思的线开始，再走到流动的情感与相通的房间。

normal.en: The root communis means shared, so to communicate is to make something shared.
normal.cn: 词根 communis 意为共有，所以 communicate 就是让某物被共同拥有。

normal.en: You communicate with a person, and you communicate an idea.
normal.cn: communicate with 接人，communicate 后也可直接接想法。

normal.en: Music communicates what a sentence cannot.
normal.cn: 音乐能传达一句话做不到的东西。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks the verb, -ion makes the noun.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 标记动词，换成 -ion 就成了名词。

normal.en: Two rooms that communicate share a door, not a wall.
normal.cn: 相通的房间共享一扇门，而不是一堵墙。

abstract.en: Picture a wire humming between two windows.
abstract.cn: 想象一根电线在两扇窗之间嗡鸣。

abstract.en: Picture a face saying more than a long letter.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸比一封长信说得更多。

abstract.en: Picture a small door hidden in a thick wall.
abstract.cn: 想象厚墙上藏着一扇小门。

examples.en: They communicate through short messages every day.
examples.cn: 他们每天靠短消息交流。

examples.en: A good teacher communicates ideas simply.
examples.cn: 好老师能把想法讲得简单明白。

examples.en: The kitchen communicates with the dining room.
examples.cn: 厨房与餐厅相通。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 communicate 记成 com（一起）加 mun（共有）加 icate：把东西变成大家共有，就是交流传达。

root: 源自拉丁语 communicare（分享），词根 communis 意为共有，本义是使某物为大家共同拥有，后引申为交流、表达与相通。

sensesIntro.en: From sharing facts, to sharing feelings, and finally to rooms that share an opening.
sensesIntro.cn: 从分享事实，到分享感受，再到共享一个开口的房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line laid between two points so that meaning can pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：两端之间架起一条能让意思顺利通过的电话线。

branches.en: Sharing information is the core modern sense.
branches.cn: 分享信息是现代核心义项。

branches.en: Feelings travel the same line as facts.
branches.cn: 情感与事实走的是同一条线路。

branches.en: Connected rooms show the physical origin of sharing.
branches.cn: 相通的房间体现了「共享」的物理来源。

branches.en: Both a fact and a feeling need a listener to be complete.
branches.cn: 事实与感受都需要一个听者才算完成。

branches.en: A passage and a message both let something through.
branches.cn: 通道与消息都让某物通过。

intro.en: Communicate is a verb base whose family grows with -ion, -ive, -or and -able.
intro.cn: communicate 是动词词基，家族靠 -ion、-ive、-or 与 -able 扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin communis, shared, also gives common, community and communism.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis（共有）也给出了 common、community 与 communism。

items.example: She communicates with the team each morning.
items.exampleCN: 她每天早上与团队沟通。

items.example: The plan was communicated to all staff.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划已传达到全体员工。

items.example: They are communicating by sign language.

items.meaning: the act or system of sharing information
items.exampleCN: 清晰的沟通能避免错误。
他是个愿意说话的孩子。

items.meaning: a person who shares ideas well
items.exampleCN: 她是一位出色的沟通者。

items.example: A communication gap caused the delay.
items.exampleCN: 沟通上的隔阂造成了延误。

definition_en: the act of sharing information, a message that is sent, or the systems used to send information
core_image: 两端之间那条不停传递消息的线
scene: 山里信号断了，救援队与外界失去联系。Good communication kept the team working as one.
sceneCN: 这里 communication 指「沟通；交流」（第 1 个义项：信息的交换）；句意是良好的沟通让这支队伍如同一人般协作。

senses.title: The act of exchanging information
senses.definition: the process of giving and receiving information between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间互相传递与接收信息的过程
senses.example: Clear communication prevents many mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 清晰的沟通能避免许多错误。
senses.why: The -ion ending turns the verb into the whole process it names.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ion 把动词变成了它所指的整个过程。

senses.title: A message
senses.definition: a message or piece of information that is sent to someone
senses.definitionCN: 发送给某人的消息或信息
senses.example: The office received a communication from the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室收到了银行的一封来函。
senses.why: One act of sharing produces one thing shared, and that thing takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一次分享产生一个被分享的东西，那个东西也用了同一个名字。

senses.title: Systems of sending information
senses.definition: the equipment and networks used to send information over distance
senses.definitionCN: 用于远距离传送信息的设备与网络
senses.example: The storm cut off all communication with the island.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨切断了与这座岛的所有通讯。
senses.why: As technology grew, the word spread from the act to the wires and signals.
senses.whyCN: 随着技术发展，这个词从动作扩展到了线路与信号。

intro.en: Communication is the noun of communicate, built on Latin communicare, to share.
intro.cn: communication 是 communicate 的名词形式，词根为拉丁语 communicare（分享）。

items.en: Communis meant common, and communicare meant to make common.
items.cn: communis 意为共有，communicare 意为使成为共有。

items.en: Communicatio named the act of sharing or exchanging.
items.cn: communicatio 指分享或交换的行为。

items.en: Old French communication kept the sense of mutual sharing.
items.cn: 古法语 communication 保留了互相分享的含义。

items.en: English communication first meant common possession or exchange.
items.cn: 英语 communication 最初指共同拥有或交换。

items.en: It now covers speech, writing, media and entire networks.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖说话、书写、媒体与整套网络。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns from the same verb family, while the meaning group names contact and correspondence.
note.cn: 形近组收的是同一动词家族的名词，近义组列出联络与往来。

entries.definition: willing to talk and share ideas
an act of honouring a memory
a person who shares ideas well
the act of giving and receiving
the state of touching or talking to someone
letters exchanged between people

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two people understanding each other, then move to a single message and to the wires of a network.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两人彼此理解开始，再走到一条消息与网络的线路。

normal.en: Communication is what happens when a message arrives and is understood.
normal.cn: 消息抵达并被理解，沟通才算发生。

normal.en: In the plural communications often means the technology of sending news.
normal.cn: 复数形式常指传递消息的技术。

normal.en: Communication skills are judged by the listener, not the speaker.
normal.cn: 沟通技巧的评判者是听者，而不是说者。

normal.en: A storm that cuts communication cuts a whole island off.
normal.cn: 一场切断通讯的风暴，会把整座岛隔绝起来。

normal.en: Change -tion to -te and the verb communicate appears.
normal.cn: 把 -tion 换成 -te，动词 communicate 就出现了。

abstract.en: Picture two people drawing the same shape on paper.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人在纸上画出同一个图形。

abstract.en: Picture a single letter crossing an ocean.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信横渡大洋。

abstract.en: Picture an antenna on a hill pointing at the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象山顶上一根指向天空的天线。

examples.en: Good communication kept the team working as one.
examples.cn: 良好的沟通让这支队伍如同一人般协作。

examples.en: The school sent a communication to every parent.
examples.cn: 学校给每位家长发了一份通知。

examples.en: The storm cut off communication with the island.
examples.cn: 暴风雨切断了与这座岛的通讯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 communication 记成 communicate（交流）加 ion（过程）：把信息变成大家共有的过程，就是沟通。

root: 由 communicate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，词根上溯拉丁语 communis（共有）与 communicare（分享），本义是共享的过程。

sensesIntro.en: From the process of sharing, to one shared message, and finally to the networks that carry it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从分享的过程，到一条被分享的消息，再到承载它的网络。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line between two points that keeps carrying messages.
core.cn: 核心意象：两端之间那条不停传递消息的线。

branches.en: The process sense is the broadest and most used.
branches.cn: 过程义最宽泛，也用得最多。

branches.en: One message is a single unit produced by that process.
branches.cn: 一条消息是这个过程产出的单个单位。

branches.en: Technology turned the process into cables, towers and networks.
branches.cn: 技术把这个过程变成了电缆、铁塔与网络。

branches.en: A message only counts once the sharing is complete.
branches.cn: 消息只有在分享完成时才算数。

branches.en: Every network exists to carry one message at a time.
branches.cn: 每个网络存在的意义，都是一次送一条消息。

intro.en: Communication is a -tion noun whose family circles around communicate.
intro.cn: communication 是带 -tion 的名词，家族围绕 communicate 展开。

latinIntro.en: The Latin communis, shared, links communication with common and community.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis（共有）把 communication 与 common、community 连在一起。

items.meaning: systems and technologies for sending information
items.example: The company runs its own communications network.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司自建通讯网络。

items.example: The class is lively and communicative.
items.exampleCN: 这个班活跃又善于交流。

items.meaning: a person who gets ideas across
items.example: A leader must be a clear communicator.
items.exampleCN: 领导者必须善于清楚表达。

items.meaning: able to be passed from one to another
a failure to understand each other
items.exampleCN: 一次沟通失误让会议推迟了。

items.example: A communication gap split the two teams.
items.exampleCN: 沟通隔阂让两支队伍分裂了。

definition_en: a group of people who live in the same area or share the same interest, religion or way of life
core_image: 一条街上的人共用同一口水井，彼此点头问好
scene: 小区里，邻居们一起清理被风吹倒的树枝。The whole community came out to clear the fallen branches.
sceneCN: 这里 community 指「社区」（第 1 个义项：住在同一片地方的人）；句意是整个社区的人都出来清理倒下的树枝。

senses.title: People of one area
senses.definition: the people who live in one particular area and often share services
senses.definitionCN: 住在某一地区、常常共用设施的一群人
senses.example: The whole community uses the new sports ground.
senses.exampleCN: 整个社区都在使用这块新运动场。
senses.why: People who live close by share roads, shops and schools, so they form a natural unit.
senses.whyCN: 住得近的人共用道路、商店和学校，自然就形成了一个单位。

senses.title: A group with one interest
senses.definition: a group of people who share an interest, a religion or a job
senses.definitionCN: 因共同的兴趣、信仰或职业而聚在一起的一群人
senses.example: She joined the online community for young writers.
senses.exampleCN: 她加入了年轻写作者的线上社群。
senses.why: Shared interest, not shared space, holds this group together.
senses.whyCN: 把这群人连在一起的是共同兴趣，而不是同一片地方。

senses.title: A feeling of belonging
senses.definition: the feeling that you belong to a group and care about its members
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己属于某个群体并关心其成员的感觉
senses.example: The small school has a real sense of community.
senses.exampleCN: 这所小学校有一种真切的归属感。
senses.why: From shared life comes a shared identity, which people also call community.
senses.whyCN: 共同生活生出共同的身份感，人们也把这叫作 community。

intro.en: Community comes from Latin communis, meaning shared or common, and first named a body of people who held things in common.
intro.cn: community 来自拉丁语 communis，意为共有的、公共的，最初指共同拥有某些东西的一群人。

items.en: Communis meant shared by many, not owned by one.
items.cn: communis 意为由许多人共有，而非一人独享。

items.en: Communitas named the state of sharing and the group that shared.
items.cn: communitas 指共有状态，也指共有东西的那群人。

items.en: Old French communete carried the word into everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 communete 把这个词带进日常使用。

items.en: English community first meant a body of people with common rights.
items.cn: 英语 community 最初指享有共同权利的一群人。

items.en: It now covers neighbourhoods, online groups and the international community.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖邻里、线上群体以及国际社会。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the shape of community, and the meaning group names other ways of speaking about people who belong together.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 community 形似的词，近义组列出其他指一群人彼此归属的说法。

entries.definition: a group of people who live together and share everything
entries.definitionCN: 共同生活、共享一切的公社

entries.definition: a political system in which property belongs to the state
to share news or feelings with others
people living together in an organised way
the area around the place where you live
a number of people or things gathered together

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a shared well, then move to shared interests and to the feeling of belonging.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从共用一口井开始，再走到共同兴趣与归属感。

normal.en: Com- means together, so a community is people held together by something.
normal.cn: com- 表示一起，所以 community 就是被某种东西连在一起的人。

normal.en: Same street gives one kind of community; same hobby gives another.
normal.cn: 同一条街是一种社区，同一个爱好是另一种社区。

normal.en: You can belong to a community without living in it.
normal.cn: 你不必住在其中，也能属于一个社群。

normal.en: Commune and community share the same old root of sharing.
normal.cn: commune 与 community 共享同一个表示共有的古老词根。

normal.en: A sense of community is the warm feeling, not the map.

intro.en: Community is built on the Latin base commun- plus the noun ending -ity.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis 提供了「共有」这一核心意思。

definition_zh: v. 通勤；减刑 n. 通勤路程
definition_en: to travel regularly to and from work
core_image: 清晨地铁站里一排排赶着上班的人
scene: 她每天坐地铁通勤到市中心上班。She commutes to the city centre by subway every day.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commute 指通勤；句意是她每天坐地铁通勤到市中心上班。

senses.title: To travel to work regularly
senses.definition: to make the same journey to work and back each day
senses.definitionCN: 每天往返同一段上班路程
senses.example: He commutes an hour each way.
senses.exampleCN: 他单程通勤一小时。
senses.why: Latin commutare means to exchange.

senses.title: To reduce a punishment

senses.example: The governor commuted the sentence.

definition_zh: adj. 紧凑的，小巧的 v. 压紧 n. 小粉盒；协定
definition_en: small and neatly fitted into a little space
core_image: 一台折叠相机塞进外套口袋
scene: 这台相机很紧凑，能装进口袋。The camera is compact enough to fit in a pocket.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：compact 指紧凑的；句意是这台相机很紧凑，能装进口袋。

senses.title: Small and neatly fitted
senses.definition: small but arranged to use space well
senses.definitionCN: 体积小而空间利用得当
senses.example: The flat has a compact kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓有个紧凑的厨房。
senses.why: Latin compactus means fastened together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 compactus 意为紧紧固定。

senses.title: To press firmly together
senses.definition: to press something into a smaller, solid mass
senses.definitionCN: 把东西压成更小更实的块
senses.example: The snow was compacted into ice.
senses.exampleCN: 雪被压成了冰。
senses.why: The verb keeps the image of pressing tight.
senses.whyCN: 动词义保留了「压紧」的意象。

senses.title: A small case or a formal agreement
senses.definition: a small container for powder, or a formal deal between parties
senses.definitionCN: 装粉的小盒，或双方正式的约定
senses.example: She opened her compact to check her hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她打开粉盒理了理头发。
senses.why: The noun has two separate lives in English.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在英语中有两条独立的用法。

intro.en: Compact joins a prefix meaning together to a verb meaning fasten.
intro.cn: compact 把表示「一起」的前缀与表示「固定」的动词连在一起。

items.en: Pangere means to fasten or fix.
items.cn: pangere 意为固定。

items.en: Compingere means to fasten together.

items.en: Compactus means fastened together.
items.cn: compactus 意为紧紧相连。

items.en: English borrowed it as an adjective.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借作形容词。

items.en: Compact now sells small and neat.
items.cn: 现代设计用 compact 表示小巧。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -pact ending; the near-meaning group names close packing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -pact 结尾；近义组列出紧密之意。

normal.en: Compactus means fastened together.

abstract.en: A city built upward.

abstract.en: Snow packed by boots.

examples.cn: 他们买了一辆适合城市的小车。

examples.cn: 双方签署了贸易协定。

root: 拉丁 com（一起）+ pangere（固定）→ compactus（紧连）→ 英语 compact

sensesIntro.en: Small, pressed, or formally agreed, all from the idea of being bound tight.
sensesIntro.cn: 小巧、压紧、签订，都源自「紧紧绑在一起」。

branches.en: A car that fits narrow streets.

definition_en: a person who spends time with you or travels with you, or a thing that goes with another
core_image: 旅途中并肩走着的两个人，一左一右踩着同一段影子
scene: 雨夜里，老人把伞往同伴那边偏了偏。He walked slowly so his companion could keep up.
sceneCN: 这里 companion 指「同伴」（第 1 个义项：与你同行的人）；句意是他放慢脚步，好让同伴跟上。

senses.title: A person who goes with you
senses.definition: a person who spends time with you or goes somewhere with you
senses.definitionCN: 与你共度时光或一同前往某处的人
senses.example: Her dog was her only companion on long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 长距离散步时，她的狗是唯一的同伴。
senses.why: A companion is defined by shared time, not by a shared address.
senses.whyCN: 同伴由共度的时光来定义，而不是由同一个住址来定义。

senses.title: A thing that matches another
senses.definition: one of a pair of things that are designed to go together
senses.definitionCN: 设计上成对、配套使用的事物之一
senses.example: This book is a companion to the earlier dictionary.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是早前那部词典的配套卷。
senses.why: Objects, like people, can be paired so that each answers the other.
senses.whyCN: 物件和人都能配对，彼此呼应。

senses.title: A handbook for a place
senses.definition: a book that gives information for visitors or users
senses.definitionCN: 为访客或使用者提供信息的书
senses.example: He bought a companion to the old city.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一本古城指南。
senses.why: A guide walks beside you in words, so it is called a companion.
senses.whyCN: 指南用文字陪你走，所以也被叫作 companion。

intro.en: Companion comes from Latin com, together, and panis, bread: a companion was the person who shared your bread.
intro.cn: companion 来自拉丁语 com（一起）与 panis（面包）：companion 本指与你分面包的人。

items.en: Com panis described one who ate bread with another.
items.cn: com panis 指与另一个人一同吃面包的人。

items.en: Companio named a fellow soldier who shared the daily ration.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 companio 指分食每日口粮的战友。

items.en: Old French compaignon widened the word to any comrade.
items.cn: 古法语 compaignon 把这个词扩展到任何伙伴。

items.en: English companion first meant a person who shared a journey.
items.cn: 英语 companion 最初指共走一段路的人。

items.en: It grew to cover matching books and travel guides.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到配套的书与旅行指南。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to companion, and the meaning group names other people or things that stay beside you.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 companion 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他陪伴在侧的人或物。

normal.en: Com- is together and pan- is bread, so a companion is a bread mate.

normal.en: A companion shares your time, not necessarily your home.

normal.en: A companion volume is a book paired with another book.

normal.en: A travel guide is a companion because it goes with you.

normal.en: Companionship is the warm noun behind the person.
normal.cn: companionship 是这个人背后那个温暖的抽象名词。

abstract.cn: 想象雨中两个人同撑一把伞。

abstract.en: Picture a dog waiting by the door every evening.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗每天傍晚在门口等候。

abstract.en: Picture two books standing side by side on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象两本书并排立在书架上。

examples.en: Her sister was her closest companion during the trip.
examples.cn: 旅途中她妹妹是她最亲近的同伴。

examples.en: The old man's companion was a small grey cat.

examples.en: This workbook is a companion to the main text.
examples.cn: 这本练习册是主教材的配套用书。

definition_en: similar enough to be compared with something else, or good enough to be equal to it
core_image: 两把并排放在桌上的尺子，长度几乎一样
scene: 同事把两份方案的报价摊在桌上逐项对照。The two plans are comparable in cost but not in speed.
sceneCN: 这里 comparable 指「可比较的；相当的」（第 1 个义项：能够放在一起比较）；句意是两份方案在成本上相当，在速度上却不同。

pos.zh: 可比较的；类似的；相当的

senses.title: Able to be compared
senses.definition: similar enough in size, value or quality to be compared
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、价值或质量上相似到可以相互比较
senses.example: The two cities are comparable in size.
senses.exampleCN: 这两座城市规模相当。
senses.why: Comparison only works when the two sides stand on common ground.
senses.whyCN: 比较只有在双方有共同基准时才成立。

senses.title: Good enough to match
senses.definition: as good as another thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类事物一样好
senses.example: Her salary is comparable to that of a senior engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的薪水相当于一名高级工程师。
senses.why: From being measurable, the word moves to being equal in worth.
senses.whyCN: 从「可以量」进一步引申为「价值相当」。

intro.en: Comparable comes from Latin comparare, to pair things as equals, built on par, equal.
intro.cn: comparable 来自拉丁语 comparare，意为把事物作为同等者放在一起，词基 par 表示相等。

items.en: Par meant equal, level, of the same rank.
items.cn: par 表示相等、齐平、同级。

items.en: Comparare meant to set two things side by side as equals.
items.cn: comparare 意为把两样东西作为同等者并排放置。

items.en: Old French comparer kept the pairing sense.
items.cn: 古法语 comparer 保留了配对比较的意思。

items.en: English comparable first described things of equal measure.
items.cn: 英语 comparable 最初描述分量相等的事物。

items.en: It now covers costs, data and any fair comparison.

normal.en: Com- is together and par is equal, so comparable means able to stand level.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，par 是相等，comparable 就是能并肩站平。

normal.en: Two things must share a measure before they are comparable.
normal.cn: 两样东西先有共同尺度，才谈得上可比。

normal.en: Compare is the verb, comparison the noun, comparable the adjective.

normal.en: In- turns it around: incomparable means beyond any rival.
normal.cn: 加上 in- 就反过来：incomparable 指无可比拟。

normal.en: A comparable salary is not the same salary, only a fair one.

abstract.en: Picture two runners crossing the line almost together.

examples.en: The two schools are comparable in size and reputation.

examples.en: We need comparable data before we choose.

root: 源自拉丁语 comparare（并列比较），词基 par 表示相等，本义是能作为同等者并排放置，后引申为类似的、相当的。

sensesIntro.en: From being fit to compare, to being equal in worth.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rulers of almost the same length lying side by side.

branches.en: Being measurable is what makes two things comparable.
branches.cn: 可被同一尺度衡量，才使两物可比。

branches.en: Value, not only size, can also be comparable.
branches.cn: 不只大小，价值也可以是相当的。

branches.en: Both senses need a common measure, one of size and one of worth.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 comparare 给英语带来一整族词：compare、comparison、comparative 与 comparable。

core_image: 两件东西放上同一台天平，一端翘起，一端下沉

sceneCN: 这里 comparative 指「比较的」（第 1 个义项：以比较为基础的）；句意是这项比较研究显示两种方法之间有明显差异。

senses.title: Based on comparison
senses.definition: relating to or based on a comparison between things
senses.definitionCN: 与事物之间的比较有关的或以比较为基础的
senses.example: The team carried out a comparative study of two diets.
senses.exampleCN: 团队对两种饮食做了比较研究。
senses.why: The ending -ive marks an adjective that describes a way of looking at things.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 标志着一个形容词，用来描述一种观察事物的方式。

senses.title: Measured against something else
senses.definition: true only when measured against something else
senses.definitionCN: 只有与别的事物相对衡量时才成立
senses.example: The country enjoys a comparative advantage in cheap labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在廉价劳动力上有相对优势。
senses.why: What is large here may be small elsewhere, so the word keeps a sense of scale.
senses.whyCN: 此处的大在别处可能就小，所以这个词带着尺度感。

senses.title: The grammar form
senses.definition: the form of an adjective or adverb that compares two things
senses.definitionCN: 形容词或副词用于比较两者的形式
senses.example: Taller is the comparative of tall.
senses.exampleCN: taller 是 tall 的比较级。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for the form that sets two things side by side.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了这个词，指把两者并排的形式。

intro.en: Comparative comes from Latin comparativus, an adjective built on comparare, to set things side by side.
intro.cn: comparative 来自拉丁语 comparativus，这个形容词由 comparare（把事物并排放置）构成。

items.en: Comparare meant to set things side by side as equals.
items.cn: comparare 意为把事物作为同等者并排放置。

items.en: Comparativus described what belongs to comparison.
items.cn: comparativus 描述属于比较的东西。

items.en: Old French comparatif entered grammar talk.

items.en: English comparative first described grammar forms.

items.en: It now also labels studies that compare two systems.
items.cn: 如今它也用来标记比较两个体系的研究。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the other members of the compare family, and the meaning group names words for things judged in relation to others.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 compare 家族的其他成员，近义组列出表示相对衡量的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a balance, then move to studies that compare and to the grammar form that sets two things side by side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从天平开始，再走到比较研究以及把两者并排的语法形式。

normal.en: Comparative keeps the idea of a balance: each side is read against the other.
normal.cn: comparative 保留了天平的意象：两边互相参照着读。

normal.en: A comparative study puts two cases in one frame.
normal.cn: 比较研究就是把两个案例放进同一个框架。

normal.en: Comparative advantage means you are better only relative to others.
normal.cn: 比较优势意味着你只是相对别人更强。

normal.en: In grammar, comparative is the middle step before the superlative.
normal.cn: 在语法里，比较级是最高级之前的中间一步。

normal.en: Comparatively is the adverb that softens a claim.
normal.cn: comparatively 是那个让说法变软的副词。

abstract.en: Picture two weights rocking a balance slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象两块砝码让天平缓缓摇摆。

abstract.en: Picture two reports spread open on one desk.
abstract.cn: 想象两份报告摊在同一张桌上。

abstract.en: Picture the word taller standing between tall and tallest.
abstract.cn: 想象 taller 站在 tall 与 tallest 之间。

examples.en: The book offers a comparative view of two legal systems.
examples.cn: 这本书对两种法律制度作了比较性的考察。

examples.en: In comparative terms, the second plan is cheaper.
examples.cn: 相对而言，第二个方案更便宜。

examples.en: Faster is the comparative of fast.
examples.cn: faster 是 fast 的比较级。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comparative 记成 compare（比较）加 ative：带着比较意味的，就是比较的、相对的。

root: 源自拉丁语 comparare（并列比较）与 comparativus，本义是属于比较的，后引申为相对的，并被语法借指比较级。

sensesIntro.en: From a method of study, to a way of measuring, and finally to a grammar form.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一种研究方法，到一种衡量方式，最后到一种语法形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two objects on one balance, one side rising as the other falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：两件东西放上同一台天平，一端翘起，一端下沉。

branches.en: The adjective first describes a method of study.
branches.cn: 这个形容词最初描述一种研究方法。

branches.en: Nothing is large in itself; it is large only in relation.
branches.cn: 没有什么本身就是大的，只有相对而言才大。

branches.en: Grammar takes the word for the form that weighs two things.
branches.cn: 语法借用这个词，指衡量两者的形式。

branches.en: A comparative study is also a study in relative worth.
branches.cn: 比较研究同时也是对相对价值的研究。

branches.en: Both judge one item against another.
branches.cn: 两者都是拿一项去对照另一项。

intro.en: Comparative adds the ending -ive to the base of compare, marking an adjective.
intro.cn: comparative 在 compare 的词基上加后缀 -ive，构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin comparare is the common source of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 comparare 是这一整族词的共同来源。

items.example: The chart lists the comparatives of ten adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 图表列出了十个形容词的比较级。

items.example: Compared with last year, sales doubled.
items.exampleCN: 与去年相比，销量翻了一倍。

items.meaning: the act of setting side by side
items.exampleCN: 交换比较笔记对两队都有帮助。

items.example: The view is incomparable at sunset.
items.exampleCN: 日落时的景色无可比拟。

definition_zh: 相对地；比较而言；通过比较（方法）；较为；相对数量上；相对价格上
definition_en: when judged by comparison with something else; relatively; by means of comparison
core_image: 两个人站上同一块背景板，标尺一拉，才知道谁其实更高
scene: 这里冬天温和，可比起南方，仍然冷得让人缩手。Winters here are comparatively mild, though next to the south they still make your hands curl.
sceneCN: 这里 comparatively 是「相对地、比较而言」（第 1 个义项：与别的情形对照后才成立的程度）；句意：这里冬天相对温和，但比起南方仍冷得让人缩手。图中可辨识物件：温度计、两地对照照片、标尺、围巾、地图。

pos.zh: 相对地；比较而言；用比较方法

senses.title: Relatively
senses.definition: in a way that is true only when measured against something else
senses.definitionCN: 只有与别物对照才成立的程度
senses.example: The region is comparatively dry.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区相对干燥。
senses.why: This is the core use: a statement is true not absolutely but against a baseline. The adverb always points to an unspoken comparison, and the hearer must supply it.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心用法：陈述不是绝对成立，而是相对于某基线成立。副词总指向一个未说出的比较，听者须自行补上。

senses.title: Comparatively speaking
senses.definition: as a discourse marker introducing a comparison
senses.definitionCN: 作为引入比较的话语标记
senses.example: Comparatively speaking, the second plan is safer.
senses.exampleCN: 比较而言，第二个方案更安全。
senses.why: Here the adverb manages the conversation: it warns that the next claim is scaled, not absolute. It softens commitment and often invites the hearer to agree on the frame.
senses.whyCN: 此处副词管理对话：它提醒接下来的主张是相对尺度，而非绝对。它软化承诺，且常邀听者认同该框架。

senses.title: By comparative method
senses.definition: by studying two or more cases side by side in order to find differences and patterns
senses.definitionCN: 并置研究两个或更多案例以找差异与模式
senses.example: The two languages were studied comparatively.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种语言被比较地研究。
senses.why: This is methodological: comparison is the instrument, not a hedge. Linguistics, anatomy, and sociology all use the adverb to name a technique that produces evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这是方法论的：比较是工具，不是模糊限制。语言学、解剖学与社会学都用该副词命名一种产生证据的技术。

senses.title: Somewhat; fairly
senses.titleCN: 较为；相对地（修饰形容词）
senses.definition: to a moderate degree when seen against the usual level
senses.definitionCN: 相对于通常水平达到中等程度
senses.example: The exam was comparatively easy.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考试较为容易。
senses.why: The adverb scales an adjective: easy compared with what? Usually with other exams or with expectations. It is a hedge that still makes a claim.
senses.whyCN: 副词给形容词定标：相对于什么算容易？通常是相对于其他考试或预期。它仍是作出主张的模糊限制。

senses.title: In relatively small number
senses.definition: in a smaller number than the relevant alternative
senses.definitionCN: 比相关对照在数量上更少
senses.example: Comparatively few students chose the course.
senses.exampleCN: 相对较少的学生选了这门课。
senses.why: Quantity is where the missing baseline matters most. 'Few' alone is vague; 'comparatively few' says the number is low for this class of case, and the class is the hidden comparison.
senses.whyCN: 数量处最见缺失基线的重要性。单说 few 模糊；comparatively few 说该数目对此类情形偏低，而“此类”就是隐藏的比较项。

senses.title: At a relatively low cost
senses.definition: at a lower price than the usual or alternative option
senses.definitionCN: 比通常或替代选择价格更低
senses.example: Housing is comparatively cheap here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里住房相对便宜。
senses.why: Economic comparisons are usually local and time-bound: cheap compared with the capital, or with last year. The adverb does not say cheap in itself, and prices are never cheap in themselves.
senses.whyCN: 经济比较通常受地点与时间限制：比首都便宜，或比去年便宜。副词不说本身便宜，而价格从不本身便宜。

senses.title: Of relatively greater importance
senses.definition: more important than other items in the same comparison
senses.definitionCN: 在同一比较中比其他项更重要
senses.example: This point is comparatively important.
senses.exampleCN: 这一点相对重要。
senses.why: Evaluation uses the adverb to rank without absolute claims. It can also weaken a point by suggesting it matters only next to something lesser, which is why tone matters.
senses.whyCN: 评价用该副词排序而不作绝对主张。它也可能通过暗示“只是比更小者重要”来削弱论点，故语气重要。

senses.title: Relatively recently
senses.definition: in a period closer to now than the comparison period
senses.definitionCN: 比对照时段更接近现在
senses.example: The technique was developed comparatively recently.
senses.exampleCN: 该技术是相对较近才发展起来的。
senses.why: Time comparisons need an anchor: recent compared with the field's history, not with last week. The adverb makes the anchor implicit, and confusion arises when hearers pick a different one.
senses.whyCN: 时间比较需要锚点：相对于该领域历史算近，而非相对于上周。副词把锚点隐含，听者选了不同锚点时便生混淆。

senses.title: In relative proportion
senses.definition: as a share that is larger or smaller than the comparison share
senses.definitionCN: 作为比对照份额更大或更小的比例
senses.example: A comparatively large share of the budget goes to health.
senses.exampleCN: 预算中相对较大的一份用于卫生。
senses.why: Proportional use adds a denominator. The share may be large while the total is small; the adverb compares ratios, not raw amounts, and that distinction is often the whole argument.
senses.whyCN: 比例用法加了分母。份额可以很大而总额很小；副词比较的是比率而非绝对量，这一区分常是争论的全部。

intro.en: Comparatively is comparative plus -ly. Comparative comes from Latin comparativus, from comparare 'to pair, match', com- plus par 'equal'. The -ive suffix is Latin -ivus; -ly is the English adverb ending. The word's meaning is not 'in a comparing manner' only but 'when compared', a use that grew in the 17C alongside scientific and statistical writing. Note the contrast with comparably: comparably means 'in a similar or equal measure', while comparatively means 'relatively, by comparison'.
intro.cn: comparatively 是 comparative 加 -ly。comparative 出自拉丁 comparativus，源于 comparare“配对、匹敌”（com- 加 par“相等”）。-ive 是拉丁 -ivus；-ly 是英语副词后缀。其义不只是“以比较的方式”，更是“经比较看来”，这一用法随十七世纪科学与统计写作而增长。注意与 comparably 的对照：comparably 指“以相似或相等的程度”，comparatively 指“相对地、经比较”。

items.en: par 'equal' underlies comparare 'to pair or match', the source of the whole family.
items.cn: par“相等”是 comparare“配对、匹敌”的词基，也是整族的来源。

items.en: comparativus 'of comparison' adds -ivus to the stem; English keeps it as -ive.
items.cn: comparativus“比较的”在词干上加 -ivus；英语保留为 -ive。

items.en: The grammatical 'comparative degree' (bigger, more careful) is named from the same adjective in the 16C.
items.cn: 语法上的“比较级”（bigger、more careful）在十六世纪由同一形容词得名。

items.en: The adverb comparatively develops the sense 'when compared, relatively', especially in science and travel writing.
items.cn: 十七世纪副词 comparatively 发展出“经比较看来、相对地”义，尤见于科学与游记写作。

items.en: Statistics and economics make it a standard hedge for figures that need a baseline.
items.cn: 十九世纪统计与经济学使它成为需要基线的数字的标准限定语。

items.en: Modern usage splits it from comparably: comparatively = relatively; comparably = in a similar measure.
items.cn: 现代用法把它与 comparably 分开：comparatively 表相对；comparably 表相似程度。

note.en: The first group is the compare family with its -ive and -able branches; the second is adverbs of degree and relation, which differ in whether they hedge, rank, or measure.
note.cn: 第一组是 compare 词族的 -ive 与 -able 两支；第二组是程度与关系副词，差别在于模糊限制、排序还是测量。

entries.definition: involving comparison; the grammar form marking 'more'.
entries.definitionCN: 比较的；语法中表“更”的形式。

entries.definition: in a similar or equal measure.
the act of comparing two or more things.
entries.definitionCN: 比较两个或更多事物的行为。

entries.definition: in relation to something else; comparatively. It is the closest synonym and often interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于他物；比较地。最近的同义词，常可互换。

entries.definition: to a moderate degree, without saying what it is compared with.
entries.definitionCN: 达到中等程度，不说与何物比较。

entries.definition: to a moderate degree, often with approval. It scales but does not point to a baseline.
entries.definitionCN: 达到中等程度，常带赞许。它定标但不指向基线。

normalIntro.en: Real links: par 'equal', comparare 'match', the -ive adjective and -ly adverb, and the modern split from comparably.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：par“相等”、comparare“匹敌”、-ive 形容词与 -ly 副词，以及现代与 comparably 的分工。

normal.en: Comparative is the adjective of comparison; add -ly and it becomes 'by comparison', not 'equally'.
normal.cn: comparative 是比较的形容词；加 -ly 后是“经比较”，不是“相等地”。

normal.en: Comparatively cheap means cheap next to something; comparably cheap means cheap to a similar degree. One letter, two baselines.
normal.cn: comparatively cheap 指相对某物便宜；comparably cheap 指便宜到相似程度。一个字母，两种基线。

normal.en: The adverb always hides a 'than what?'. If the hearer cannot fill it, the sentence is incomplete.
normal.cn: 该副词总藏着“比什么？”。听者填不上，句子就不完整。

normal.en: In grammar the 'comparative degree' is the -er/more form; the same adjective names both the grammar and the method.
normal.cn: 语法中“比较级”是 -er/more 形式；同一形容词既命名语法，也命名方法。

normal.en: par 'equal' is still alive in parity and peer; comparison is the act of putting equals side by side.
normal.cn: par“相等”仍活在 parity 与 peer；比较就是把对等者并排放。

abstract.en: Relativity in language is a hedge and a claim at once: it lowers the volume but still asserts a difference.
abstract.cn: 语言中的相对性同时是模糊限制与主张：它降低音量，却仍断言差异。

abstract.en: The missing baseline is where speakers disagree; 'comparatively' hides a choice that can be contested.
abstract.cn: 缺失的基线正是说话者分歧之处；comparatively 藏着一个可被质疑的选择。

abstract.en: Comparison creates a scale, and a scale turns difference into a judgement of more or less.
abstract.cn: 比较创造尺度，而尺度把差异变成多少的判断。

examples.en: The winters here are comparatively mild.
examples.cn: 这里的冬天相对温和。

examples.en: Comparatively speaking, the risk is small.
examples.cn: 相对来说，风险很小。

examples.en: Comparatively few firms survived the crisis.
examples.cn: 相对较少的企业挺过了危机。

dict_mnemonic.text: “康帕拉提夫利”——先 compare 一下，再说话 → comparatively 相对地

root: comparative（拉丁 comparativus ← comparare“配对、匹敌”= com-“一起”+ par“相等”）+ -ly。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of comparatively: relatively, as a discourse marker, by comparative method, somewhat, in small number, at low cost, of greater importance, recently, and in relative proportion. Every one of them hides a baseline that the hearer must supply.
sensesIntro.cn: comparatively 的九个义项：相对地、作为话语标记、用比较方法、较为、数量少、价格低、更重要、时间较近、比例上。每一个都藏着听者须补上的基线。

branches.en: THE HEDGE: the core relative use and the discourse marker both soften an absolute claim.
branches.cn: 模糊限制：核心相对义与话语标记都软化绝对主张。

branches.en: THE METHOD: comparison as an instrument that produces evidence.
branches.cn: 方法：比较作为产生证据的工具。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: easy, few, cheap are all scaled against a usual level.
branches.cn: 程度：容易、少、便宜都相对于通常水平定标。

branches.en: THE RANK AND THE SHARE: importance and proportion compare positions or ratios, not raw amounts.
branches.cn: 排序与份额：重要性与比例比较位置或比率，而非绝对量。

branches.en: THE TIME: 'recently' needs the field's history as its anchor.
branches.cn: 时间：“较近”需要以该领域历史为锚。

intro.en: Comparatively is comparative + -ly. Comparative is Latin comparativus, from comparare, com- plus par. Its family includes comparison, comparable, comparably, and comparability; par also gives parity and peer.
intro.cn: comparatively 是 comparative 加 -ly。comparative 是拉丁 comparativus，出自 comparare（com- 加 par）。词族含 comparison、comparable、comparably、comparability；par 还给出 parity 与 peer。

latinIntro.en: Latin comparare 'match' gives comparativus 'of comparison'. English keeps -ive for the adjective and adds -ly for the adverb. The same stem yields comparatio, hence comparison, and comparabilis, hence comparable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 comparare“匹敌”给出 comparativus“比较的”。英语保留 -ive 作形容词，加 -ly 作副词。同一词干给出 comparatio（即 comparison）与 comparabilis（即 comparable）。

items.meaningCN: 比较的；比较级（-ative 形容词）

definition_en: to examine two or more things to see how they are alike or different, or to say that one thing is like another
core_image: 把两只手伸到眼前，左右反复端详
scene: 买鞋的姑娘把两只鞋翻过来看鞋底和走线。She compared the two pairs before choosing.
sceneCN: 这里 compare 指「比较；对比」（第 1 个义项：查看异同）；句意是她在挑选之前把两双鞋比了比。

senses.title: To look for differences
senses.definition: to examine two things to see how they are alike or different
senses.definitionCN: 查看两样事物有何相同与不同
senses.example: Compare the two maps and mark the changes.
senses.exampleCN: 比较这两张地图，标出变化。
senses.why: The core act is setting two things on the same footing to judge them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心动作是把两物放在同一基准上判断。

senses.title: To say one thing is like another
senses.definition: to describe one thing as being like another
senses.definitionCN: 把一物描述成与另一物相似
senses.example: The poet compares the moon to a silver coin.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人把月亮比作一枚银币。
senses.why: Once things are side by side, the mind easily turns one into a picture of the other.
senses.whyCN: 两物一旦并置，人就容易把一物想象成另一物的样子。

senses.title: To be worth matching
senses.definition: to be good enough to be mentioned beside another
senses.definitionCN: 好到可以与另一者并列提及
senses.example: No singer can compare with her.
senses.exampleCN: 没有歌手能和她相比。
senses.why: Comparison can end in a verdict that two things are not equal.
senses.whyCN: 比较可以得出两者并不对等的结论。

intro.en: Compare comes from Latin comparare, to bring two things together as equals, from com, together, and par, equal.
intro.cn: compare 来自拉丁语 comparare，意为把两样东西作为同等者带到一起，由 com（一起）与 par（相等）构成。

items.en: Par meant equal, level, of the same standing.
items.cn: par 表示相等、齐平、地位相同。

items.en: Comparare meant to place two things side by side.
items.cn: comparare 意为把两样东西并排放置。

items.en: Old French comparer kept the plain everyday sense.
items.cn: 古法语 comparer 保留了朴素的日常含义。

items.en: English compare first meant to match one thing against another.
items.cn: 英语 compare 最初指拿一物去对照另一物。

items.en: It gained the softer sense of likening one thing to another.
items.cn: 后来它又添了把一物比作另一物的柔和含义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short verbs that differ from compare by one or two letters, and the meaning group names other verbs of matching and setting against.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compare 只差一两个字母的短动词，近义组列出其他表示对照与比配的动词。

entries.definition: to force someone to do something
to collect material into one work
to obey a rule or request
to show differences between two things
to describe one thing as similar to another
to be equal to another thing

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two hands held up to the eye, then move to likening and to being worth a place beside another.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从把两样东西举到眼前开始，再走到比作以及值得与之一比。

normal.en: Com- is together and par is equal, so compare means to weigh two things as equals.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，par 是相等，compare 就是把两样东西当同等者来称。

normal.en: Compare with looks at difference; compare to makes a picture.
normal.cn: compare with 看差异，compare to 造比喻。

normal.en: Shop around and compare prices before you pay.
normal.cn: 付钱之前多走几家，比一比价格。

normal.en: Two friends compare notes after a test.
normal.cn: 考完试，两个朋友交换一下看法。

normal.en: Beyond compare means nothing can stand beside it.
normal.cn: beyond compare 指没有东西能与它相比。

abstract.en: Picture two apples held up one in each hand.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手各举一个苹果。

abstract.en: Picture a poet pointing at the moon and then at a coin.
abstract.cn: 想象诗人先指月亮，再指一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a list of prices with two columns side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价目表，两列数字并排。

examples.en: Compare the two answers before you decide.
examples.cn: 决定之前先比较这两个答案。

examples.en: He compared her smile to morning light.
examples.cn: 他把她的微笑比作晨光。

examples.en: Few cities can compare with Paris for food.
examples.cn: 论美食，很少有城市能与巴黎相比。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compare 记成 com（一起）加 pare（看作相等）：把两样东西放在一起看成同等，就是比较。

root: 源自拉丁语 comparare，com- 表示一起，par 表示相等，本义是把事物作为同等者并列审视，后引申为比较与比作。

sensesIntro.en: From checking two things, to likening one to another, and finally to being worthy of comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 从查考两样东西，到把一物比作另一物，最后到值得与之相比。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands held at eye level, turning objects over side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：把两只手伸到眼前，左右反复端详两样东西。

branches.en: The plain act of checking two things is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 查看两样东西这个朴素动作是最古老的义项。

branches.en: Likening grows out of the same side-by-side picture.
branches.cn: 比作正是从同一个并置的画面里长出来的。

branches.en: A comparison can also end with one side clearly ahead.
branches.cn: 比较也可以以一方明显领先收尾。

branches.en: Both put two things in one frame, one to judge, one to picture.
branches.cn: 两者都把两物放进同一画框，一个为判断，一个为想象。

branches.en: You cannot say who is better without first comparing.
branches.cn: 不先比较，就说不出谁更好。

intro.en: Compare is a free base from Latin comparare; endings mark its tense and its relatives.
intro.cn: compare 是来自拉丁语 comparare 的自由词基，词尾变化标记时态，也生成同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin par, equal, is the small root that holds the family together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 par（相等）是把这个词族系在一起的小词根。

items.example: Compared with last spring, prices fell.
items.exampleCN: 与去年春天相比，价格下降了。

items.meaning: the act of setting side by side

items.meaning: the act or result of comparing

definition_zh: 比较；对比；比喻；可比之处
definition_en: the act of comparing two or more things, or a statement that one thing is like another
core_image: 桌上摊开两张地图，手指在相同的位置来回移动
scene: 导购把两款手机的参数列在同一张纸上。The comparison made the choice much easier.
sceneCN: 这里 comparison 指「比较」（第 1 个义项：把事物放在一起对照）；句意是这番比较让选择容易多了。

senses.title: The act of comparing
senses.definition: the act of examining two or more things to see how they differ
senses.definitionCN: 检查两样或更多事物以看出差别的行为
senses.example: A comparison of the two reports shows one clear error.
senses.exampleCN: 对比两份报告，能看出一个明显错误。
senses.why: The noun names the whole act, from first look to final judgement.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指整个过程，从最初一看直到最后判断。

senses.title: A stated likeness
senses.definition: a statement that one thing is like another
senses.definitionCN: 说一物像另一物的表述
senses.example: The poem uses a comparison between life and a journey.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗把人生比作一段旅程。
senses.why: When two things are held together long enough, one becomes an image of the other.
senses.whyCN: 两物并置久了，一物就成了另一物的形象。

senses.title: A basis for judging
senses.definition: the way two things can be measured against each other
senses.definitionCN: 两物可以相互衡量的方式
senses.example: There is no comparison between the two teams this season.
senses.exampleCN: 本赛季这两支队伍没法相提并论。
senses.why: The word also names the standard itself, the ground on which a judgement is made.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指标准本身，即作出判断所依据的基准。

intro.en: Comparison comes from Latin comparatio, the noun of comparare, to set things side by side.
intro.cn: comparison 来自拉丁语 comparatio，是 comparare（把事物并排放置）的名词形式。

items.en: Comparare meant to weigh two things against each other.
items.cn: comparare 意为让两样东西相互衡量。

items.en: Comparatio named the act and the result of that weighing.
items.cn: comparatio 指这种衡量的动作与结果。

items.en: Old French comparaison carried the noun into common use.
items.cn: 古法语 comparaison 把这个名词带进日常使用。

items.en: English comparison first meant a setting of two things together.
items.cn: 英语 comparison 最初指把两样东西放在一起。

items.en: It grew to cover figures of speech and fair grounds for judging.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到修辞上的比喻与公平判断的依据。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that share the shape of comparison, and the meaning group names other ways of contrasting or drawing a parallel.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 comparison 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示对照或类比的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two maps on one table, then move to a spoken likeness and to the ground of a fair judgement.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从桌上两张地图开始，再走到说出的比喻与公平判断的基准。

normal.en: Comparison is the noun of compare: the act turned into a thing.
normal.cn: comparison 是 compare 的名词：动作变成了一件东西。

normal.en: In comparison with sets one thing beside another.
normal.cn: in comparison with 就是把一物放到另一物旁边。

normal.en: By comparison is the phrase for a quick shift of view.
normal.cn: by comparison 是快速换个视角的说法。

normal.en: A comparison can be an argument, and also a poem.
normal.cn: 比较既可以是一场论证，也可以是一句诗。

normal.en: No comparison means the gap is too wide to measure.

abstract.en: Picture two timetables held up to the window light.
abstract.cn: 想象两张时刻表举到窗前对光看。

abstract.en: Picture one finger moving between the same point on two maps.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在两张地图的同一位置来回移动。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where one pan drops and stays down.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一端沉下去，再没抬起来。

examples.en: The comparison between the two cities is unfair.
examples.cn: 这两座城市之间的比较并不公平。

examples.en: By comparison, the second route is much shorter.
examples.cn: 相比之下，第二条路线短得多。

examples.en: His performance invited comparison with the greats.
examples.cn: 他的表演让人把他与大师们相比。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comparison 记成 compare（比较）加 ison：比较这个动作落成的名词，就是比较。

root: 源自拉丁语 comparatio，由 comparare（并列比较）加名词后缀而来，本义是把事物并列衡量的动作，后引申为比喻与可比之处。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of comparing, to a stated likeness, and finally to the standard behind a judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 从比较的动作，到明确说出的类比，最后到判断背后的基准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two maps spread open, one finger moving between the same two points.

branches.en: The act itself is the plainest sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 动作本身是这个名词最朴素的义项。

branches.en: A likeness spoken aloud is a comparison made of words.
branches.cn: 说出口的相似，就是用语言做成的比较。

branches.en: Every judgement needs a standard to compare against.
branches.cn: 每个判断都需要一个可对照的标准。

branches.en: Both put two things in one frame for the mind to hold.
branches.cn: 两者都把两物放进同一画框，好让心里握住。

branches.en: The act and its standard are two halves of one judgement.
branches.cn: 比较的动作与它的标准，是同一个判断的两半。

intro.en: Comparison is built on the verb compare with the noun ending -ison.

latinIntro.en: The Latin comparatio already joined the act of weighing with its result.

scene: 火车每个隔间都坐着四名乘客。Each compartment of the train seats four passengers.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：compartment 指隔间；句意是火车每个隔间都坐着四名乘客。

senses.title: A divided space
senses.definition: one of the parts into which a space is divided
senses.definitionCN: 空间被分出来的其中一部分
senses.example: He put the tickets in a side compartment.
senses.exampleCN: 他把票放在侧面的隔层。
senses.why: Latin compartiri means to divide among people.

senses.title: A separate area of thought or life

senses.example: She keeps work in a separate compartment.

senses.why: The figurative sense treats the mind as a box.

definition_en: an instrument that shows direction, a tool for drawing circles, or the range of something
core_image: 掌心大小的圆盘上，一根磁针轻轻摆动后定住指向北方
scene: 山里起雾，队长掏出小圆盘看指针方向。Without a compass they would have walked in circles.
sceneCN: 这里 compass 指「指南针」（第 1 个义项：指示方向的仪器）；句意是没有指南针，他们就会原地绕圈。

senses.title: The direction finder
senses.definition: an instrument with a magnetic needle that always points north
senses.definitionCN: 带磁针、始终指向北方的仪器
senses.example: The compass swung and settled on north.
senses.exampleCN: 罗盘转了转，停在了北面。
senses.why: A needle that finds north gives the traveller the one fixed line everything else is measured from.
senses.whyCN: 找到北方的磁针给了旅人一条固定线，其余方向都由它量出。

senses.title: The drawing tool
senses.definition: a tool with two legs used for drawing circles
senses.definitionCN: 用来画圆的两脚工具
senses.example: He drew a perfect circle with a compass.
senses.exampleCN: 他用圆规画了一个完美的圆。
senses.why: Both meanings turn on measuring a circle or a round world, so they share one name.
senses.whyCN: 两个义项都围绕测量圆或圆形世界，所以共用一个名字。

senses.title: The range or scope
senses.definition: the limit or range of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的限度或范围
senses.example: Such a journey lies beyond the compass of one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的旅程超出了一个夏天的范围。
senses.why: A compass marks how far a circle reaches, so it came to mean any reach or limit.
senses.whyCN: 罗盘标出圆能伸到多远，于是引申为任何范围或限度。

intro.en: Compass comes from Latin com, together, and passus, a step, and first meant to pace out a circle of ground.
intro.cn: compass 来自拉丁语 com（一起）与 passus（一步），本义是按步量出一圈地面。

items.en: Passus was the length of one step.
items.cn: passus 指一步的长度。

items.en: Compassare meant to measure a space by walking round it.
items.cn: compassare 意为绕着走一圈来量一块地方。

items.en: Old French compasser kept the sense of going round.
items.cn: 古法语 compasser 保留了绕行一圈的意思。

items.en: English compass first named a circuit or a boundary.
items.cn: 英语 compass 最初指一圈或一条边界。

items.en: It moved to the needle for direction, the tool for circles and any scope.

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a needle settling on north, then move to the tool that draws circles and to any reach or limit.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从磁针定在北方开始，再走到画圆的工具以及任何范围或限度。

normal.en: Com- is together and pass means step, so a compass measures a walk in a circle.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pass 是步子，所以 compass 量的是绕一圈的路。

normal.en: One needle, one fixed north: that is why a compass calms a lost walker.
normal.cn: 一根磁针，一个固定的北方：所以罗盘能让迷路的人安心。

normal.en: Two legs and a point draw a perfect circle.

normal.en: The compass of a book is the range it covers.

normal.en: En- plus compass gives encompass, to go all the way round.
normal.cn: en- 加 compass 得到 encompass，意为整个围起来。

abstract.en: Picture a needle trembling, then holding still on north.
abstract.cn: 想象磁针抖了几下，然后定在北方不动。

abstract.en: Picture a metal point pressed into paper, a circle opening out.
abstract.cn: 想象金属尖压进纸里，一个圆慢慢张开。

abstract.en: Picture a fence that marks how far the land goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆，标出土地延伸到哪里。

examples.en: The compass needle pointed steadily north.
examples.cn: 指南针的指针稳稳地指向北方。

examples.en: Draw the circle with a compass and a pencil.

examples.en: That subject lies beyond the compass of this book.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compass 记成 com（一起）加 pass（步）：一起量步、绕行一圈，圆盘定方向，两脚画圆，也都量出范围。

root: 源自拉丁语 com（一起）与 passus（步），本义是按步量地、绕行一圈，后指量圆的工具与指示方向的罗盘，再引申为范围。

sensesIntro.en: From a needle that finds north, to a tool that draws the round world, and finally to any reach or limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 从找到北方的磁针，到画圆的工具，最后到任何范围或限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm-sized dial whose needle trembles, then holds on north.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心大小的圆盘上，一根磁针轻轻摆动后定住指向北方。

branches.en: Finding north is the sense travellers cling to.
branches.cn: 找到北方是旅人最依赖的义项。

branches.en: The drawing tool keeps the old idea of a measured circle.
branches.cn: 画圆工具保留了量出一个圆的古老想法。

branches.en: Any boundary is a circle drawn around a thing.
branches.cn: 任何边界都是围绕某物画出的一圈。

branches.en: A needle gives direction, and a boundary gives range.
branches.cn: 磁针给方向，边界给范围。

branches.en: Both senses come from one act: measuring a round space.
branches.cn: 两个义项都出自同一个动作：量出一块圆的范围。

intro.en: Compass is built on Latin com, together, plus passus, a step.
intro.cn: compass 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 passus（一步）构成。

latinIntro.en: The step base pass- also appears in passage and in bypass.
latinIntro.cn: 表示步子的词基 pass- 也出现在 passage 与 bypass 里。

definition_zh: 有同情心的；出于怜悯的；温和体恤的；（假期、宽免等）因家庭急难而特许的
definition_en: feeling or showing sympathy for people who are suffering, and wishing to help them
core_image: 一位医生查房时先坐在床沿，问的不是指标而是病人昨夜睡得怎样，手里的病历一直合着
scene: 重症病房里，医生把病历夹合上放到一边，先问病人昨晚疼得能不能睡着。The compassionate doctor sat on the edge of the bed and asked about the night before any question about test results.
sceneCN: 这里 compassionate 形容「对他人疾苦敏锐并愿意体恤的」（第 1 个义项：对他人苦难敏感而温情的）；句意为这位有同情心的医生坐在床沿，先问昨夜的情况，再谈检查结果。可辨识物件：合上的病历夹、病床床沿、监护仪、夜灯。

pos.zh: 有同情心的；出于怜悯的；体恤的

collocations.zh: 因家庭急难而准予的特别假
基于人道理由的（申请）依据
怜悯性释放（因重病或丧亲而提前释放）
温和保守主义（政治用语）

senses.title: Sensitive to other people's pain
senses.definition: describing a person who notices other people's suffering and feels for them
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人能察觉他人的痛苦并为之动情
senses.example: The compassionate doctor sat on the edge of the bed and asked about the night.
senses.exampleCN: 这位有同情心的医生坐在床沿，先问昨夜的情况。
senses.why: The adjective simply carries the noun's feeling into description: the person is full of shared suffering.
senses.whyCN: 形容词只是把名词里的那份情感带进描述：这个人心中满是与人共担的苦。

senses.title: Driven by pity
senses.definition: describing an action taken because someone's suffering has been noticed
senses.definitionCN: 形容因察觉到他人受苦而采取的行动
senses.example: A compassionate refusal is better than a careless yes.
senses.exampleCN: 出于怜悯的拒绝，胜过轻率的答应。
senses.why: When the word moves from the person to the act, it marks the motive behind the act.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从人移到行为上，它标出的是行为背后的动机。

senses.title: Gentle in manner
senses.titleCN: 语气与做法温和体贴的
senses.definition: describing words or handling that avoid adding humiliation to an already painful situation
senses.definitionCN: 形容言辞或处理方式不再给本就痛苦的处境添上羞辱
senses.example: She gave the news in a compassionate voice, without any blame in it.
senses.exampleCN: 她用体恤的语气告知消息，话里没有一丝责备。
senses.why: Compassion is not only felt but delivered; the manner of delivery can wound or spare, so the word describes tone as well.
senses.whyCN: 同情不只要被感受到，还要被传达出来；传达方式可以伤人也可以护人，所以这个词也形容语气。

senses.title: Granted for a family emergency
senses.definition: describing leave or absence allowed because of a death, illness or crisis in the family
senses.definitionCN: 形容因家人去世、重病或突发变故而被批准的假期
senses.example: He was given three days of compassionate leave after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，他获准三天急难假。
senses.why: Workplace rules borrowed the word for the one situation in which an employer is expected to put a person before a schedule.
senses.whyCN: 职场规章借用了这个词，专指雇主被期待把人排在日程之前的那种情形。

senses.title: Allowed on humane grounds
senses.definition: describing a release, transfer or exception granted because of severe personal hardship
senses.definitionCN: 形容因个人处境极为艰难而获准的释放、转院或例外
senses.example: Prisoners nearing death may apply for compassionate release.
senses.exampleCN: 临近死亡的囚犯可以申请人道释放。
senses.why: Law keeps a narrow door for cases where strict application would be cruel, and the word names that door.
senses.whyCN: 法律为严格适用会显得残忍的情形留了一道窄门，这个词就是那道门的名字。

senses.title: Care that includes feeling
senses.definition: describing treatment that attends to distress as well as to the clinical task
senses.definitionCN: 形容在完成医疗任务之外也照顾到痛苦的照护
senses.example: Compassionate care begins with asking what the patient is most afraid of.
senses.exampleCN: 有温度的照护，从问病人最害怕什么开始。
senses.why: Care work made the adjective a standard of quality, not merely a compliment.
senses.whyCN: 照护行业把这个形容词变成了质量标准，而不只是一句称赞。

senses.title: Merciful in religious language
senses.titleCN: 宗教语境中慈悲为怀的
senses.definition: in religious writing, describing a mercy that extends to all beings without condition
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教文献中，形容无条件施及一切众生的慈悲
senses.example: The tradition describes a compassionate presence that turns towards every creature.
senses.exampleCN: 这一传统描述一种转向一切生灵的慈悲临在。
senses.why: The oldest use of the family is religious, and the adjective still carries that wide, unconditional reach.
senses.whyCN: 这个词族最古老的用法是宗教性的，形容词也仍带着那种无边的、无条件的覆盖。

senses.title: Designed with hardship in mind
senses.titleCN: 制度设计上顾及疾苦的
senses.definition: describing a policy or institution built to soften the hardship it inevitably causes
senses.definitionCN: 形容某项政策或制度在设计中设法减轻它必然造成的困苦
senses.example: A compassionate policy explains the decision in plain language and offers an appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 体恤的政策用平实的语言解释决定，并提供申诉渠道。
senses.why: The word's final reach is structural: once compassion is expected of institutions, rules themselves are called compassionate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最后延伸到结构层面：一旦人们期待机构有同情心，规则本身也会被称作体恤的。

intro.en: Compassionate is the adjective formed from compassion with the Latin suffix -ate, 'having the quality of'. The noun and the adjective entered English within the same medieval period.
intro.cn: compassionate 是由 compassion 加拉丁后缀 -ate「具有……性质的」构成的形容词。名词与形容词都在中世纪进入英语。

items.en: Pati 'to suffer, endure' is the root; its participle passus also gives passion and passive. The deeper origin of pati is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 词根 pati 意为「受苦、忍受」；其分词是 passion 与 passive 的来源。pati 的更深来源属重构。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus pati formed compati, 'to suffer with', the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 pati 构成 compati「一同受苦」，这是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: The noun compassio named the state of shared feeling; English took the noun first and then built the adjective on it.
items.cn: 名词 compassio 指共感的状态；英语先借入名词，再据它造出形容词。

items.en: The ending -ate comes from Latin -atus, marking a person or thing that possesses the quality named by the stem.
items.cn: 词尾 -ate 来自拉丁 -atus，表示人或事物具有词干所指的性质。

items.en: The adjective appears in English in the sixteenth century, first in religious prose and later in ordinary description of people and acts.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十六世纪出现于英语，最早见于宗教散文，后来才用于日常对人、对事的描述。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation of the adjective is not precisely dated, and the pre-Latin root of pati has no agreed form, so any Indo-European shape for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个形容词最早的英语书证没有确切年代；pati 在拉丁语之前的词根也没有公认形式，凡给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that sit beside this one in the same Latin family or in the same sentence; group two holds adjectives with a similar warmth but a different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一拉丁词族、或在同一句里并列出现在的形容词；第二组是暖意相近但覆盖面不同的形容词。

entries.definition: From the same suffering participle but describing intense enthusiasm or love, not tenderness towards pain.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「受苦」分词，却形容炽烈的热情或爱，而非对痛苦的温柔。

entries.definition: The noun names the feeling; the adjective names the person or act that has it. The pair is a regular noun-adjective set, not two separate ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指这份情感，形容词指具有这份情感的人或行为。两者是常规的名词—形容词配对，并非两个不同概念。

entries.definition: From the present participle of the same verb, 'enduring'; a patient bears pain while a compassionate person responds to it.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该动词的现在分词，意为「忍受着」；病人承受痛苦，而有同情心的人回应痛苦。

entries.definition: Built on the Latin verb for suffering as well but in the sense of enduring together; its modern meaning is 'able to work together', which has lost the pain entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 同样建于表示「受苦」的拉丁动词，原义为「能一同承受」；现代义为「能相容并用」，痛感已完全消失。

entries.definition: Attentive to another's practical needs; it can be shown by good service alone, without any reflection on suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 留意他人实际需要；仅靠周到的服务就能体现，不必对痛苦有所体察。

entries.definition: Quick to feel for another's trouble and to express that feeling; it stops at the feeling, where compassionate goes on to help.
entries.definitionCN: 容易为他人的困难动情并表达出来；它止于情感，而 compassionate 会继续走向援手。

entries.definition: Treating people or animals in a way that avoids unnecessary suffering; it is a minimum standard, while compassionate is a warmth beyond the minimum.
entries.definitionCN: 以不造成不必要痛苦的方式对待人或动物；它是最低标准，而 compassionate 是超出最低标准的热度。

entries.definition: Gentle and careful in touch or speech; it describes the manner only, not the motive of noticing another's pain.
entries.definitionCN: 在触碰或言语上轻柔小心；它只描述方式，不含察觉他人痛苦的动机。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root, the real noun behind the adjective, the real workplace phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、形容词背后真实的名词、真实的职场说法与真实的同族词。

normal.en: The noun compassion means suffering together; the adjective simply says that a person or act has that quality.
normal.cn: 名词 compassion 意为「一同受苦」，形容词只是说明某人或某行为具备这种性质。

normal.en: The ending -ate marks possession of a quality, the same ending that turns fortune into fortunate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 表示「具有某种性质」，与把「运气」变成「幸运的」用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: Workplace phrases pin the word down: compassionate leave, compassionate grounds, compassionate release.
normal.cn: 职场说法把这个词固定下来：急难假、人道理由、怜悯性释放。

normal.en: Hospitals use it as a quality standard: compassionate care is assessed alongside technical competence.
normal.cn: 医院把它当作质量标准：有温度的照护与技术能力一起被考核。

normal.en: The contrast to hold in mind is passionate, from the same root but about heat rather than tenderness.
normal.cn: 要记住的对照是 passionate，同出一个词根，但说的是炽烈而非温柔。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that slows down before it touches a bruise.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在碰到淤青之前先放慢了速度。

abstract.en: Picture a door held open a few extra seconds for someone carrying too much.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门为提着太多东西的人多开了几秒。

abstract.en: Picture a voice that lowers itself when the news is bad.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音在坏消息面前自觉放低。

examples.en: The university granted her compassionate leave for the funeral.
examples.cn: 学校批准她因葬礼申请的急难假。

examples.en: A compassionate manager asks what happened before asking when the work will be done.
examples.cn: 体恤的管理者先问发生了什么，再问工作何时完成。

examples.en: The report recommends compassionate release for prisoners with terminal illness.
examples.cn: 报告建议对绝症囚犯实行人道释放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「共同 + 受苦 + 具有这种性质」——心里装着别人的痛，言行就自然温和体恤

root: 拉丁 compassio「同感、怜悯」+ 后缀 -ate（具有……性质的）；compassio 出自 compati「一同受苦」= com-（共同）+ pati（受苦）。深层词根不确定，印欧形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same quality applied to different things: first a person, then an act, then a tone, then a leave, a legal exception, a style of care, a religious mercy, and finally a policy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述的是同一种性质落在不同对象上：先落在人身上，再落到行为、语气、假期、法律例外、照护风格、宗教慈悲，最后落到政策上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that slows down before it reaches a place that hurts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在伸向疼痛之处前先放慢了速度。

branches.en: PERSON AND MOTIVE: the one who notices, and the act that follows from noticing.
branches.cn: 人与动机：先是察觉的人，再是由察觉引出的行为。

branches.en: DELIVERY: the same feeling shows in how the words are said.
branches.cn: 传达：同一份情感体现在话怎么说出口。

branches.en: TIME AND EXEMPTION: employers give days, the law opens a narrow door.
branches.cn: 时间与例外：雇主给出几天假，法律开出一道窄门。

branches.en: CARE AND MERCY: a clinical standard on one side, an unconditional religious reach on the other.
branches.cn: 照护与慈悲：一边是临床标准，一边是无条件的宗教覆盖。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: the quality moves from people into the design of rules.
branches.cn: 结构：这种性质从人身上移入规则的设计。

intro.en: Compassionate is built from a Latin noun plus the suffix -ate, and both parts recur in many English words.
intro.cn: compassionate 由一个拉丁名词加后缀 -ate 构成，两部分都在大量英语词中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The stem carries shared suffering; -ate marks possession of a quality, as in fortunate and passionate.
latinIntro.cn: 词干带着「共同受苦」的意思；-ate 表示具有某种性质，如 fortunate 与 passionate 中的用法。

items.example: The prefix makes the feeling shared.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀让情感成为共享的。
这个名词是形容词的基础。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成描述。

items.example: The compassionate doctor sat on the edge of the bed.
items.exampleCN: 这位有同情心的医生坐在床沿。

items.example: The ward was known for its compassionateness.
An uncompassionate reply closed the conversation.
items.exampleCN: 一句冷漠的回应终止了对话。

scene: 旧电脑屏幕上，新软件的安装进度条走到末尾。 The new software ran on the old computer and the installation bar finished without a problem, so the two were compatible.
sceneCN: 这里 compatible 是「兼容的」（第 1 个义项：设备或软件能一起正常工作）；句意：新软件在旧电脑上顺利运行，安装进度条走完没有问题，说明两者兼容。
